title: extending a Context subclass buys a class no exemption from the host-global rule
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Host Globals' (Locked): "Platform-specific globals such as `process`, `window`, `document`, filesystem, and network MUST NOT be unconditional globals in authored `.sm` code. Host functionality MUST be represented by typed capabilities, normally accessed through the inherited `Capability.context()` method." The scope is authored `.sm`, with no carve-out for the file that implements the capability. reference/capabilities.mdx, 'Platform Services': "JavaScript hosts provide live implementations; tests supply deterministic ones." compatibility.mdx, 'Source Relationship': `.ts` modules "MUST retain their own complete syntax and behavior when imported by Smithers." This is the over-correction guard for 20-host-globals/a-capability-implementation-reads-the-host-through-a-trusted-binding: the two programs differ only in whether the `Date.now()` lives in `.sm` or in the trusted `.ts` binding. Being a real `Context` subclass, being the declared capability's implementation shape, and being named like one all buy nothing, because the rule never consults any of them — the refusal is unconditional, so there is nothing for a non-implementation to claim. If a future lane ever adds an implementation-side opt-out, this case is what stops it from being claimable by ordinary code.
